compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Teams running several tracker projects against one codebase (or several repos against one ticket
store) cannot use the bridge: it is hard-wired to exactly one project at three points —
`JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`_config_schema.py`), the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair
from one key and fails closed on an empty one (`fetcher.jqls_for`), and the applier aborts a pass when
any outbound mutation targets a key outside that project (`applier.CrossProjectTargetError`). The only
escape is the destructive one-way `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`. Assignee preservation for
tracker-unresolvable users is owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff` and taken as a dependency,
not duplicated here.

(Full original description with line-anchored citations preserved verbatim as a ticket comment,
2026-08-13.)

## Approach

Model many-to-many as one shared ticket store between N repos and N tracker projects. Each ticket
records the project it syncs into and the repos it belongs to.

The STORE owns the project set — `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the tickets branch beside
`bindings.json`/`prev_snapshot.json`. Reason (mechanical): `prev_snapshot.json` is last-known-remote
state; if two repos fetched different project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would
diff the other's projects as remote deletions. A store-owned project set removes that failure mode by
construction and leaves no per-repo list to disagree.

Built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`) and the backend-neutral
port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)`, `Backend.project` / `Backend.query_project`.
`Backend.project` ("the backend's effective write/create project scope") is the per-repo default for
rebar-created tickets; no new config key; generalizes beyond Jira.

Migration writes NO events. The ticket project field is tri-state — absent=legacy, explicit-empty=
never sync, explicit key=sync there — mirroring `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths
(`docs/ticket-model.md`). Absent resolves against the legacy default recorded in the mapping, seeded by
an idempotent check-then-act ensure unit (`docs/migrations.md`, the sanctioned seam; the ordered
School-A ledger is explicitly not built). A per-ticket EDIT migration was rejected: four-figure event
writes under the store lock, and the MCP-boot entry runs the ensure sweep on a short lock budget and
skips when contended — an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three entry points.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch, cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `_store/init.py` — the ensure unit seeding the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the conditional capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `_commands/composer.py`, `_lib_writes.py`,
  `_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, and an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, and the
      same operations exist on the library and MCP surfaces; checked by a per-surface test asserting
      each of the three surfaces reads back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records the project it came from; checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair is issued
      per configured project and asserting the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; checked by an
      outbound-differ test asserting an empty mutation list for that ticket while a sibling with a
      project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets that project rather than the repo default;
      checked by a dispatch test asserting the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update targeting a project inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it
      still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired applier test covering both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; checked by a migration test asserting the store's event count is byte-identical before
      and after the sweep and that each ticket resolves to the default.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking that capability refuses writes,
      while a single-project store remains writable; checked by a store-compat test covering both.

## Child decomposition (disjoint file sets; no edit conflicts)

- **Project mapping store** — `.bridge_state/projects.json` + helpers + the ensure seed. Delivers migration/legacy-default criteria.
- **`bridge projects` command surface** — subcommand + library/MCP parity per epic `2f79`. Delivers criterion 1.
- **Ticket project field** — schema, CREATE data, reducer, create-time args on all three surfaces; promote-only rule (cannot change project of a bound ticket). Delivers empty-project criterion.
- **Ticket repos field** — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — fan-out + snapshot union; per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project. Delivers two-project fetch criterion.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create; guard relaxed from single project to set membership. Delivers explicit-project + guard criteria.
- **Store-compat capability stamp** — conditional `required_capabilities` entry + fail-closed read. Delivers final criterion.
- **Docs + ADR** — model, mapping, tri-state field, decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — LAST child: rehearse against two live Jira Cloud projects on an
  isolated tickets-branch copy on the encrypted S3 remote (capability from epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`,
  hence the depends_on); dry-run-gated, all created issues removed. Fixtures cannot reach the
  cross-project contamination failure mode this validates.
- **Module-size relief** — several files this feature edits sit within ~30 lines of the 800 hard cap.
  Behaviour-preserving extractions along existing seams, each ordered ahead of the story needing room;
  they deliver no epic criterion (preconditions; their own criteria are unchanged suite + measured LOC).

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive at every layer. Absent project = legacy; a pre-feature store behaves as today, no operator
action. A single-project store never receives the capability stamp, so older binaries keep working;
only a genuinely multi-project store fails closed on them — the intended protection (an older binary
would fetch its one project, see other projects' tickets as unbound, and create duplicates in the
wrong project). Rollback is per-change on Gerrit; the mapping and capability entry are inert to older
binaries apart from the deliberate fail-closed, and deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary
to implicit-legacy with the idempotent ensure re-stamping on the next covered write.
